nodes.label: Whisper Transcription
nodes.rationale: Video/audio cannot be read directly, so they are transcribed to text and then treated as doc files; a domain-hint prompt derived from god node labels improves transcription quality.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts changed files to save tokens and time; code-only changes skip semantic extraction entirely because AST alone is sufficient.

nodes.label: Replace-on-Re-extract
nodes.rationale: Every source_file in new_chunks is dropped from the base before merge so stale nodes do not survive; changed files are deliberately NOT passed to prune_sources or they would delete freshly re-extracted content.

nodes.label: Callbacks
nodes.rationale: Callbacks provide hooks at agent, LLM, and tool lifecycle stages for logging, monitoring, argument transformation, and result modification without modifying agent internals.

nodes.label: Callback Execution Order
nodes.rationale: Callbacks fire in a defined order: agent_start, llm_start, llm_end, tool_before, tool_after, agent_end, so multiple callbacks compose predictably.

nodes.label: Graphify Integration Rules
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions should hit the knowledge graph first via query/path/explain because the scoped subgraph is far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: The query binary has no stemming, synonyms, or cross-language matching, so the query must be expanded against actual graph vocabulary first or the literal matcher returns zero hits and the answer collapses to noise.

nodes.label: Work Memory Self-Improving Loop
nodes.rationale: Saving an outcome (useful/dead_end/corrected) closes the feedback loop so future sessions start from preferred sources and skip known dead ends.

nodes.label: Callbacks System
nodes.rationale: Callbacks hook into agent execution stages to modify tool arguments, log events, and transform responses; project-level ones auto-load while user-level ones are gated by settings.json.

nodes.label: CLI Skills System
nodes.rationale: Skills are loaded from user-level ~/.kader/skills and project-level ./.kader/skills as SKILL.md directories with YAML frontmatter.

nodes.label: Tool Confirmation System
nodes.rationale: Interactive [Y/n/reason] approval guards potentially destructive tool operations and lets users provide context when rejecting.

nodes.label: Agent Skills
nodes.rationale: Modular SKILL.md directories inject specialized domain knowledge into the system prompt and can be loaded dynamically via the skills_tool.

nodes.label: Custom Tools
nodes.rationale: User-level and project-level BaseTool subclasses extend agent capabilities and can be targeted at planner, executor, or both.

nodes.label: File System Tools with Gitignore Filtering
nodes.norm_label: file system tools with gitignore filtering
nodes.rationale: read_directory, grep, and glob automatically filter out files matching .gitignore patterns, but filtering can be disabled with apply_gitignore_filter=False.

nodes.label: Special Commands
nodes.rationale: Custom command agents defined by CONTENT.md or .md files let users encode repeatable tasks invoked with a slash command.

nodes.label: Subagents
nodes.rationale: YAML-defined specialized agents are auto-discovered and registered as AgentTools the planner can delegate to, each with isolated memory, tools, and provider.

nodes.label: YAML Agent Configuration
nodes.rationale: BaseAgent.from_yaml lets agent behavior, tools, provider, persistence, and retry settings be declared declaratively instead of in code.

nodes.label: PlannerExecutorWorkflow
nodes.rationale: The CLI is powered by a planner-executor workflow that adds reasoning, planning, and tool execution on top of the agent framework.

nodes.label: Agent-As-Tool (AgentTool)
nodes.rationale: Lets a PlanningAgent delegate work to a ReActAgent with persistent sub-agent memory and context aggregation into the main session checkpoint.

nodes.label: Planner-Executor Framework
nodes.rationale: Separates planning (Architect/PlanningAgent) from execution (Worker/ReActAgent) so complex multi-step tasks run with isolated sub-agent memory and automated context aggregation.
